headline: Bitcoin is holding near $60,000 on Sunday after falling to a two-year low, with money still leaving US bitcoin funds and a busy US data week ahead.

market.asOf: Bitcoin and ether from CoinMarketCap as reported by IT Times at 02:00 UTC on Sun 22 Nov (11:00 Korea, 09:00 Bangkok); ether's change is the figure IT Times gives. Solana from CoinMarketCap, read by this desk at about 03:59 UTC; its 24h change was +1.89% there but about +4.8% on Binance.US. Prices move fast; use the live prices on this page.
market.fearGreed: 12 out of 100, "Extreme Fear", on the Alternative.me Crypto Fear & Greed Index (read at about 03:59 UTC), the same as the day before.

stories.title: Bitcoin holds around $60,000 after a 12% weekly drop
stories.summary: Bitcoin fell to its lowest price since September 2024 early on Saturday, then bounced back to about $60,000 and stayed there through Sunday morning in Asia. It still ended the week about 12% lower, and crypto company shares fell even harder.
points: Bitcoin fell as low as $55,130, its lowest since September 2024, then rose more than 9% to about $60,300, per CoinDesk.
At 02:00 UTC on Sunday (11:00 in Korea) bitcoin was at $60,020, up 1.85% over 24 hours, per IT Times citing CoinMarketCap.
Bitcoin ended Saturday near $60,121, about 12% below $68,314 a week earlier, per CEO Economy.
Forced selling of crypto bets totalled about $1.8 billion over 24 hours per CoinDesk citing CoinGlass, and $2.67 billion over a different 24-hour window per Bitcoin.com.
Over the week Strategy (MSTR) shares fell 30.3% and Coinbase 20.1%, per CEO Economy.

sources.label: CEO Economy: crypto week in review

stories.title: US bitcoin funds lose about $1.25 billion in a week
stories.summary: Money kept flowing out of US spot bitcoin ETFs, the funds that let people buy bitcoin through a normal brokerage account. November is now on course to be the second-worst month on record, and BlackRock's fund still has not posted its Friday number.
points: On Thursday 19 Nov bitcoin ETFs lost $582.3 million, $541.1 million of it from BlackRock's IBIT, its biggest daily outflow since launch, per Cryptoticker using Farside data.
Friday 20 Nov's provisional total was -$124.5 million, with IBIT not yet published, per Cryptoticker.
November outflows are about $3.59 billion so far, second only to June 2026's $4.51 billion, per Cryptoticker.
Ether ETFs lost about $221.7 million over the week, per CEO Economy.
CoinDesk put the week's bitcoin ETF outflows at about $1.1 billion.

sources.label: CEO Economy: crypto week in review

stories.title: Stocks, US inflation data and a big options expiry set up a busy week
stories.summary: Last week's tech-led stock slide and expectations of a Fed rate hike in December helped push crypto down. This week US stocks reopen Monday, key inflation and growth data land Wednesday before Thanksgiving, and a large batch of bitcoin options expires Friday.
points: The Nasdaq fell about 10% last week, including 5.3% on Friday, per CEO Economy; CoinDesk put Friday's drop at more than 4%.
The S&P 500 is at 6,910, 11.6% below its 6 Oct record, per Cryptoticker.
October PCE inflation and Q3 GDP are both due Wed 25 Nov at 8:30am ET (20:30 Bangkok); core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year against 3.1% before, per Newsquawk.
Bitcoin options covering 112,323 BTC, about $6.76 billion, expire on Deribit on Fri 27 Nov at 08:00 UTC, per Cryptoticker (data from 21 Nov).

sources.label: CEO Economy: crypto week in review
Cryptoticker: Tether, Kraken and Monday's open

briefs.title: Kalshi faces a Monday court hearing in New York
briefs.summary: A Manhattan state court hears New York Attorney General Letitia James's request for a restraining order on Monday 23 Nov at 11:30am ET; Kalshi's lawyer says it would shut the exchange "for every customer, everywhere", and a federal judge on Friday denied the CFTC's emergency bid to block New York's case, per The Block.

briefs.title: Kraken's bitcoin-Canadian dollar market briefly crashes
briefs.summary: Kraken's BTC/CAD pair traded as low as C$24,250 on Saturday morning UTC, about 70% below Kraken's own US dollar bitcoin price, per CoinPaprika.

briefs.title: AI finds a Bitcoin Core bug; no funds at risk
briefs.summary: A medium-severity flaw let bad actors stall Bitcoin nodes for more than a dozen seconds per message; it affects versions 29.0 to 31.2 and is fixed in 30.5, 31.3 and 32.1, per Bitcoin.com.

briefs.title: Chainflip drained of $4.86 million
briefs.summary: An attacker used what looks like Chainflip's own compromised signing key to empty its Ethereum vault of about $4.86 million; FLIP fell 34% and the protocol went into safe mode, per The Block.

briefs.title: Cyber bridge exploit; Upbit and Bithumb freeze CYBER
briefs.summary: About 5.213 million CYBER tokens were minted without permission on Solana and sold for about $968,000 in ETH; Upbit and Bithumb froze CYBER deposits and withdrawals, per The Block.

briefs.title: Questions over Tether's safety cushion
briefs.summary: Tether's reported reserve buffer was $7.95 billion on 30 Sep; at Saturday's gold and bitcoin prices Cryptoticker estimates it at $2.8-3.6 billion, while USDT traded at $0.9985, per Cryptoticker.

briefs.title: XRP back above $0.90
briefs.summary: XRP was at $0.9307 on Sunday morning in Asia, up 2.41% over 24 hours, per IT Times citing CoinMarketCap.

briefs.title: Wells Fargo is the biggest reported bitcoin ETF holder
briefs.summary: US institutions held a record 356,491 BTC through ETFs on 30 Sep, with Wells Fargo the largest at 30,553 BTC-equivalent; these are positions from before the recent selling, per Bitcoin.com citing Galaxy.

calendar.note: MBG on Sunday 22, SOON on Monday 23, MON (the largest, about 16.6 billion tokens worth about $220M on this desk's data) and SOSO on Tuesday 24, XPL and H on Wednesday 25, HUMA on Thursday 26, SIGN, PROS and GRASS on Saturday 28, and FF and CARDS on Sunday 29 November. See the unlock table on this page for sizes, dates and confidence. (Dates from this desk's unlock data.)
October's manufacturing reading was 54.9, per FinancialJuice.

calendar.event: New York court hearing on Kalshi
calendar.note: Justice Melissa Crane hears the New York Attorney General's request for a restraining order; Kalshi says it could shut its exchange nationwide, per The Block.
October came in at 91.7, per FinancialJuice.

calendar.event: Dell, HP Inc and Workday earnings
calendar.note: Dell's call is at 4:30pm ET (04:30 Bangkok); analysts expect revenue of about $50.63 billion and earnings of $6.63 a share, per Finviz. HP's call is at 5:00pm ET (05:00 Bangkok), per HP.

calendar.event: US PCE inflation (Oct), Q3 GDP (second estimate), durable goods and jobless claims
calendar.note: Core PCE is expected at 3.2% a year (prior 3.1%), per Newsquawk. Q3 GDP is expected at 3.5% against the 3.4% first estimate, per Trading Economics. Weekly jobless claims come out on Wednesday this week, per FinanceCalendar; the last reading was 203K, per Stock Analysis.
The Fed's survey of business conditions around the country, per the Fed's calendar. October new home sales come out earlier the same day at 10:00am ET (22:00 Bangkok), per the Census Bureau.
On Friday 27 Nov US stocks close early at 1:00pm ET (01:00 Sat Bangkok), per NYSE. Crypto trades all day, but thin trading can mean bigger swings.

calendar.event: Monthly bitcoin options expiry on Deribit
calendar.note: About $6.76 billion of bitcoin options (112,323 BTC) expire, with the "max pain" level at $73,000, per Cryptoticker using Deribit data from 21 Nov.
The last jobs report before the Fed decision, per the BLS schedule. November CPI is Thu 10 Dec, the day after the Fed.

calendar.event: Next Fed meeting and rate decision
calendar.note: Two-day meeting 8-9 Dec with new projections; the statement is at 2:00pm ET Wed 9 Dec (02:00 Thu 10 Dec Bangkok), per the Fed. Fed officials stop public comment on policy from Sat 28 Nov, per the Fed's blackout rules.
